$comment: The Sunim Crew base, schema only. No rows, no data, nothing of anyone's.
Create it with: npm run base:create
The Development field is the point of the whole thing. It is a formula,
so nobody can set it: it reads the evidence fields and computes the
stage. If you build this base by hand, that field must be a formula.
Field NAMES are what the crew addresses. A duplicated base keeps the
names and gets new ids, and the crew resolves names to ids at startup.
name: Sunim Design System

tables.name: Components
tables.description: One row per component. The status is derived, never typed in.

tables.name: Storybook Testing
tables.description: One row per test case. A row with no screenshot does not count.

$comment: These cannot be created through the API in one pass, because they
depend on the tables existing first. Add them by hand, once.
The script prints these instructions when it finishes.
rollups: Components: Total Tests, a count of linked Storybook Testing rows
Components: Passed Tests, a rollup counting rows whose result is Passed
Components: Synchronization %, a formula of your choosing

$comment: The stage, derived from evidence. Adjust the field names if you
renamed any, and keep the order: a part-done fix round is Fixing,
developmentFormula.formula: IF(AND({Production URL}, {Astro Link}), 'Completed', IF(AND({Total Tests} > 0, {Failed Tests} = 0, {Retest Tests} > 0), 'Fixed', IF(AND({Retest Tests} > 0, {Failed Tests} > 0), 'Fixing', IF({Failed Tests} > 0, 'To be fixed', IF(AND({Total Tests} > 0, {Passed Tests} = {Total Tests}), 'To be deployed', IF({Storybook}, 'Ready for Testing', IF({Commit}, 'To be staged', 'To-do')))))))
